hoses: Hydrant supply hose from hydrant to Engine 181 intake
Monitor Supply Line A: 300 ft of 2½-inch hose from Engine 181 discharge to portable monitor
Monitor Supply Line B: 300 ft of 2½-inch hose from Engine 181 discharge to portable monitor
nozzles: Portable monitor with 1⅜-inch smooth bore tip, 500 GPM @ 80 PSI
appliances: Portable monitor positioned uphill from Engine 181; use appliance loss stated by the problem
sceneElements.elevation: Portable monitor is 60 ft above Engine 181; use the stated 0.5 PSI/ft training approximation

problems.title: Flow Per Monitor Supply Line
problems.question: The elevated portable monitor is flowing 500 GPM total and is supplied by two equal hose lines from Engine 181. The two lines split the monitor flow; they do not each flow the full monitor total. What flow should be used for each supply line?
formulaBreakdown: Two equal supply lines split the flow.
problems.instructorExplanation: For a two-line monitor supply, calculate friction loss per line using the 250 GPM in each line.
problems.explainMistake: Do not enter the 500 GPM total when the question asks for flow in each individual line.

problems.title: Friction Loss Per Supply Line
problems.question: Each elevated-monitor supply line is 300 ft of 2½-inch hose. The monitor flows 500 GPM total through two equal lines, so calculate each line at one-half of the total flow. Using FL = C × (GPM/100)² × (length/100), with C = 2, what is the friction loss in each supply line?
problems.instructorExplanation: Each supply line carries 250 GPM; either equal line has about 40 PSI friction loss.
problems.explainMistake: Do not calculate one supply line at the full 500 GPM monitor flow.

problems.title: Elevation Pressure
problems.question: The portable monitor is positioned 60 ft above Engine 181. For this training problem, use 0.5 PSI per foot of elevation gain. What elevation pressure must be added?
formulaBreakdown: Training elevation pressure = 60 ft × 0.5 PSI/ft = 30 PSI.
problems.instructorExplanation: The stated training approximation adds 30 PSI for a 60-ft uphill elevation gain.
problems.explainMistake: For an uphill operation, add—not subtract—the stated elevation allowance.

problems.title: Portable Monitor Pump Discharge Pressure
problems.question: Engine 181 is supplying an uphill portable monitor with two equal 300 ft 2½-inch supply lines. The monitor flows 500 GPM total; split the flow equally between the two lines for friction-loss calculations. The monitor uses 80 PSI nozzle pressure, has a stated 25 PSI monitor appliance loss, and is 60 ft above the pump. Use the training elevation approximation of 0.5 PSI/ft. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: Use one equal supply path's friction loss, then add nozzle pressure, the stated elevation allowance, and the stated appliance loss.
problems.explainMistake: Do not add both parallel line friction losses together.

problems.title: Hydrant Supply Line Count
problems.question: The operation has one hydrant supply line connected to Engine 181’s intake and two separate discharge lines supplying the portable monitor. For water-supply tracking, count only intake-side hydrant supply lines feeding Engine 181. How many hydrant supply lines feed Engine 181?
formulaBreakdown: One hydrant supply hose is connected to Engine 181.
problems.instructorExplanation: The two monitor hoses are discharges, not intake-side hydrant supply lines.
problems.explainMistake: Do not count the two monitor discharge lines as hydrant supply lines.
